name: Material 3
fit: Cross-platform apps that generate color, type, and elevation from one source color.
principles: One visual language across platforms, with room for a product's own brand. Color roles come from a source color. Surfaces stack by elevation. Motion explains where an element came from.
color: Dynamic roles: primary, secondary, tertiary, surface, outline, and error, each with a container and an on-color. Light and dark schemes are generated from the same roles.
typography: A type scale from display through headline, title, body, and label, in large, medium, and small.
spacing: Padding and gap follow a 4px rhythm. Window margins change by window-size class.
shape: A shape scale from none to full, applied per component corner.
elevation: Tonal elevation. Higher surfaces are a lighter tint in the light scheme and a lighter overlay in the dark scheme, not only a drop shadow.
layout: Canonical layouts and window-size classes for compact, medium, and expanded.
icons: Material Symbols, with weight, grade, and optical size.
components: Buttons, FAB, navigation bar and rail, top app bar, sheets, dialogs, lists, chips, and text fields, with pressed and dragged states.
themes: Light and dark, plus contrast variants. A single source color retints the scheme.
adapt: Keep the role model, the type scale, and tonal elevation. Choose a source color and type that belong to this product. Drop Android-only patterns on the web.
